reportedSymptom: Attribute measured CPU observations to the application's culture-sensitive dictionary lookup work without assuming which framework or native function is expensive.
groundTruth: The repository owns two distinct lookup entrypoints. Each route must return correct results and own measured on-CPU stacks only in its active phase. Inclusive workload ownership is not exclusive managed or native leaf cost; neither comparer is required to remain slower.

workload.setup: Launch a fresh Release BadCodeSample per phase over loopback. Windows ETW kernel profiling requires elevation and resolution of the project-owned managed entrypoints. Explicit OS mode; no EventPipe fallback.
workload.activation: Capture two separate 8-second windows: sustained culture-sensitive requests, then sustained ordinal requests in a fresh process. Verify every completed response and require reciprocal positive/negative method ownership.
workload.cleanup: Cancel each phase's load and terminate its sample process before starting the other phase.

misleadingSignals: An inclusive lookup entrypoint owns a sampled call path, not the exclusive CPU of its descendants.
A resolved framework ancestor or ICU module total does not prove native hashing function boundaries.
Runtime names, inlining, algorithm choices and relative comparer costs can legitimately change.
